lead:
FIFA and CAF ordered the Nigeria Football Federation to suspend its election process immediately while they assess the leadership crisis in Nigerian football, halting the elective congress planned for 27 September in Lafia.

The day in brief: in Oyo, police said six children taken by a suspected trafficking ring died in captivity, while 17 were rescued and seven suspects arrested. A three-storey commercial building in Wuse Zone 4, Abuja, collapsed hours after officials sealed it. NDC figures condemned the reported blockade of Peter Obi's convoy in Benue. The national security adviser's office said 1,487 terrorists were killed in July and August, and statistics showed the petrol import bill jumped nearly elevenfold in the second quarter to N952 billion. The Dangote refinery said its N2.15 trillion IPO aims to reach 10 million investors through the BVN system, six Nigerian companies joined the FTSE Frontier 50 index, and the government opened exclusive talks with APM Terminals on the Badagry port. On the pitch, the Falconets lost their World Cup opener to Spain, and the Super Eagles agreed to play Russia in October.

items.h: FIFA and CAF suspend NFF election process
items.s: In a letter dated 7 September signed by FIFA chief member associations officer Elkhan Mammadov, FIFA and CAF ordered the NFF to suspend its electoral process with immediate effect, ending the elective congress set for 27 September in Lafia, Nasarawa. The two bodies will send a joint mission to Abuja to assess the legal and governance issues behind the crisis.

items.h: Six trafficked children die in captivity as police rescue 17 in Oyo
items.s: Oyo police said six children abducted by a suspected child-stealing and trafficking syndicate died in captivity, while 17 were rescued and seven suspects arrested after an intelligence-led investigation into a network moving children across state lines. One suspect, Adejoke Popoola, allegedly confessed to selling two sets of her own children, including newborn twins for N300,000.

items.h: Abuja building collapses hours after it was sealed
items.s: A three-storey commercial building in Wuse Zone 4, Abuja, collapsed at about 7.20pm on Monday, hours after FCT development control officials reportedly sealed it and ordered occupants out. The FCT Emergency Management Department and fire service began search and rescue amid uncertainty over how many people were affected.

items.h: Obi's convoy reportedly blocked in Benue
items.s: NDC figures condemned the reported attack and blockade of Peter Obi's convoy in Benue as he tried to reach Yelwata. Benue deputy governorship candidate Raymond Edoh urged international bodies to take note, and Kogi East senatorial candidate Peter Ameh called it “ridiculous and unacceptable” and asked the police and DSS chiefs to call governors to order.

items.h: ONSA says 1,487 terrorists killed in two months
items.s: The Office of the National Security Adviser said operations in July and August killed 1,487 terrorists and reflected an increasingly coordinated, intelligence-driven approach to terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and arms trafficking, in a quarterly update by Chido Onumah, an adviser to the NSA.

items.h: Petrol import bill jumps 989% to N952bn in second quarter
items.s: NBS trade data show Nigeria spent N952.15 billion on petrol imports in the second quarter of 2026, up 989.4 per cent from N87.40 billion in the first quarter, despite increased local refining. The bill was still 59.9 per cent lower than the N2.38 trillion of a year earlier.

items.h: Dangote refinery aims for 10 million investors in N2.15trn IPO
items.s: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery said its IPO, valued at about N2.15 trillion or $1.6 billion and due to open on 14 September, targets up to 10 million Nigerian investors through a secure subscription process linked to the Bank Verification Number system.

items.h: INEC to launch real-time election readiness tracker
items.s: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan said the commission will roll out a real-time readiness tracker to monitor preparations for the 2027 elections in all 36 states and the FCT. In Rivers, the Rainbow Coalition denied claims that it is working with INEC.

items.h: Tinubu mourns State House media official who died in Kano
items.s: President Tinubu mourned Peter Onwubuariri, 48, an assistant director of media at the State House and a former News Agency of Nigeria journalist, who died in Kano on Monday after a prolonged illness. His wife Catherine said he had been in hospital for about a month.

items.h: Police enforce Lagos judgment in Tinubu land dispute
items.s: Police began enforcing a Lagos High Court judgment in a long-running dispute over 114.476 hectares in Ogombo village, Eti-Osa, after Justice Olukayode Ogunjobi adopted terms of settlement between interests connected to the estate of Iyalode Efunroye Tinubu and members of the Kosoko royal family.

items.h: Gunmen kill three vigilantes in Kaduna
items.s: Gunmen killed three members of the Kaduna State Vigilance Service, including its deputy commander there, on the Zuntu-Zaria road in Kubau at about 12.20am on Monday while they were conducting stop-and-search on the highway.

items.h: Bandits kill vigilante and abduct resident in Kano village
items.s: Bandits stormed Dakwara village in Gwarzo, Kano, at about 4am on Tuesday, firing sporadically and demanding motorcycles, the village head Usman Ibrahim said. They killed a vigilante, Abdulmuminu Bichila, who tried to rescue a boy they had seized, and abducted a resident.

items.h: Troops rescue 12 civilians in Zamfara
items.s: Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma rescued 12 civilians in separate operations in Kaura Namoda and Tsafe, Zamfara, including after responding to a distress call when terrorists infiltrated a community in Kaura Namoda.

items.h: Katsina governor presents N828.6bn 2027 budget
items.s: Governor Dikko Radda presented a N828.64 billion 2027 budget to the Katsina Assembly, N69.23 billion or 7.71 per cent less than the approved 2026 budget, with N637.91 billion, nearly 77 per cent, for capital spending. Speaker Nasir Yahaya Daura pledged quick passage.

items.h: Super Eagles to play Russia in October friendly
items.s: The NFF confirmed the Super Eagles will play Russia, currently banned from FIFA competitions, in a friendly at the 44,000-seat Nizhny Novgorod Stadium on 6 October. The teams drew 1-1 in Moscow in June 2025.

items.h: Falconets lose 2-0 to Spain in World Cup opener
items.s: The Falconets lost 2-0 to Spain, the 2022 champions, in their opening match of the FIFA U20 Women's World Cup at the Arena Sosnowiec, Poland. Marisa Garcia scored past goalkeeper Christiana Uzoma in the 13th minute.

items.h: Eguavoen named interim Super Falcons coach
items.s: Former Super Eagles coach Augustine Eguavoen will lead the Super Falcons on an interim basis in their 2028 Olympic qualifiers against Comoros in October, assisted by Christopher Danjuma, while the NFF searches for a permanent coach.

items.h: CBN makes terrorism financing a supervisory priority
items.s: The CBN said it has made terrorism financing a current supervisory priority to stop illicit actors exploiting the financial system, its acting communications director Hakama Sidi-Ali said.

items.h: Six Nigerian firms make FTSE Frontier 50 index
items.s: FTSE Russell included six Nigerian companies, FirstHoldCo, Zenith Bank, GTCO, Dangote Cement, Aradel and MTN Nigeria, in its FTSE Frontier 50 index from 18 September, as Nigeria prepares to return to frontier market status after three years.

items.h: FG begins exclusive talks with APM Terminals on Badagry port
items.s: Marine and Blue Economy Minister Adegboyega Oyetola said the government has begun exclusive talks with APM Terminals on the proposed Badagry deep seaport, after the Maersk unit signed a memorandum with Badagry Port Development in Copenhagen during his visit.

items.h: Grid operator holds hearing on DisCos' market debts
items.s: The Nigerian Independent System Operator concluded a public hearing from 1 to 4 September with distribution companies on their unpaid obligations to the electricity market, told them to begin settling immediately and threatened sanctions. DisCos' June collections fell 7.82 per cent to N191.86 billion.

items.h: NMDPRA denies under-remitting gas flare penalties
items.s: The NMDPRA denied the Auditor-General's finding that gas flare penalties were under-remitted to the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, saying the variances arise from timing and reconciliation in the Federation Account, not a shortfall.

items.h: Crude nears $100, raising fears of petrol price rise
items.s: Brent crude traded at $98.05 a barrel on Tuesday morning, up 2.11 per cent, renewing fears of another round of pump price increases and raising the prospect that the Dangote refinery would soon revise its gantry price.

items.h: Atiku blames Tinubu for foreign investors' exit and heavy borrowing
items.s: Atiku Abubakar said the flight of foreign portfolio investment shown in the latest Nigerian Exchange data is a “vote of no confidence” in the government's economic management. “Capital votes with its feet,” he said, questioning domestic borrowing despite higher oil prices.

items.h: Fayemi likens Atiku's subsidy pledge to a campaign ploy
items.s: Former Ekiti governor Kayode Fayemi told Arise TV that Atiku's pledge to restore the petrol subsidy is a strategy to exploit hardship for votes, likening it to the APC's adoption of a Muslim-Muslim ticket in 2023.

items.h: APC figure asks agencies to probe Atiku allegations
items.s: Hilliard Eta, a former APC national vice chairman, urged the EFCC and other agencies to investigate financial crime allegations against Atiku Abubakar. Atiku's spokesman Phrank Shaibu dismissed them as recycled claims revived for political purposes.

items.h: Osun tribunal starts hearing; APC legal team disowns petition
items.s: The Osun governorship election tribunal began proceedings, displaying petitions in the names of the APC and PDP against Governor Ademola Adeleke's re-election in the 15 August election, but the APC's legal team in the state disowned the petition filed in the party's name.

items.h: NDC denies illegal payments in candidate selection
items.s: The Nigeria Democratic Congress denied claims of illegal payments and favouritism in choosing its 2027 candidates, calling them deliberate misinformation by disgruntled people, spokesman Osa Director said.

items.h: Kwara defectors say PDP offers a better platform
items.s: APC members who defected to the PDP in Offa, Kwara, led by Ezekiel Adepoju, said the opposition party offers a better platform for the state's political future.

items.h: Lagos APC opens 2027 mobilisation for Tinubu
items.s: At a rally in Lagos, APC leaders said re-electing President Tinubu is in the national interest and that he has lived up to expectations in a complex country. Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu said the party will take no voter for granted.

items.h: Rivers ADC tells Wike intimidation will not win elections
items.s: The ADC in Rivers rejected FCT Minister Nyesom Wike's claim that its vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, will be defeated by noon on election day, saying only INEC can announce results and intimidation will not win elections.

items.h: Shettima calls for peaceful, issue-based campaign
items.s: Inaugurating a national transporters' structure for Tinubu/Shettima 2027 in Abuja, Vice President Kashim Shettima said the President is committed to transport infrastructure to ease the work of transporters, and urged peaceful, issue-based campaigning.

items.h: Churches back state police to tackle insecurity
items.s: The Spiritual Advisory Council of Christ Church, a body of the Anglican, Methodist and Presbyterian churches, backed state police and urged full implementation to tackle insecurity. Its Port Harcourt council also demanded free and fair elections and condemned ostentatious displays amid hardship.

items.h: Plateau sends medical supplies to diphtheria treatment centres
items.s: Plateau Governor Caleb Mutfwang ordered drugs and medical supplies sent immediately to facilities treating diphtheria patients, including Jos University Teaching Hospital, said Kim Jerry Bot, head of the state drug and medical commodities agency.

items.h: ONSA starts multi-agency crisis response drill in Delta
items.s: The national security adviser's office began “Rapid Response 3”, a multi-agency crisis response exercise in Asaba running to 11 September, to test agencies' readiness for complex emergencies, said Rear Admiral Adedotun Ayo-Vaughan of the Presidential Command and Control Centre.

items.h: Nigerian scientist wins $100,000 NLNG prize for AI MRI tool
items.s: Nigerian AI researcher Mary Brenda Akoda won the $100,000 2026 Nigeria Prize for Science and Innovation, sponsored by NLNG, for GenScan AI, a tool that cuts the time needed for MRI scans, judges chaired by former minister Omobola Johnson announced in Lagos.

items.h: Oxford names MDCN head Fatima Kyari visiting fellow
items.s: The University of Oxford named Professor Fatima Kyari, registrar of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria, its 2026 Aig-Imoukhuede Visiting Fellow. She will spend six months at the Blavatnik School of Government studying how Nigeria can expand medical training.

items.h: Credit guarantee company mobilises N46.95bn in first year
items.s: The National Credit Guarantee Company said it unlocked N46.95 billion in credit in its first year, using N21.59 billion of guarantees to help 19 lenders, including 13 commercial banks, reach 67,512 borrowers in 25 states and the FCT.

items.h: Enugu palm firm invests $2.2m in refinery
items.s: Enugu United Palm Products, a partnership between Pragmatic Palms and the Enugu government, began commercial production and is investing $2.2 million in a refinery to turn crude palm oil into olein and stearin and refine palm kernel oil. Governor Peter Mbah praised the revival of dormant assets.

items.h: Customs officer dies in Cross River crash
items.s: Etteng Ise, 54, a Customs officer at the Mfum border, died in a lone crash near Alesi village on the Ikom-Calabar highway at about 2.56pm on Monday after losing control of his car while avoiding a pothole, police said.

items.h: Bauchi police arrest seven over Dass clashes
items.s: Bauchi police said seven suspects are in custody for alleged conspiracy, inciting disturbance and culpable homicide over the 4 September clashes in Dass that killed two people, spokesman Nafiu Habib said.

items.h: Yusuf Alli says Intermediate Games will expose athlete poaching
items.s: Former Olympian Yusuf Alli said EKO 2026, the first National Intermediate Games for athletes aged 15 to 18, running in Lagos from 1 to 15 October, will show which states develop grassroots talent and which simply recruit established athletes.
